sections.overview: The West Indian manatee inhabits warm coastal waters from the southeastern United States and Caribbean to northeastern Brazil.
sections.identification: It is a large, gray-brown aquatic mammal with foreflippers and a broad, paddle-shaped tail.
sections.habitat: It uses coastal, estuarine and river habitats in marine, brackish and fresh water, often where aquatic vegetation is abundant.
sections.diet: It is herbivorous and grazes on submerged, floating and emergent aquatic plants.
sections.behavior: Manatees may spend up to eight hours a day feeding and surface regularly to breathe.
sections.reproduction: Gestation lasts about 12–15 months, and a calf may remain dependent on its mother for one to two years.
sections.ecology: Two subspecies are recognized: the Florida manatee and the Antillean manatee; see the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service account for their ranges.
sections.conservation: Mexico lists the Antillean subspecies as endangered under its national standard.
